text: January 17, 2026 - The Central Franconian languages, also referred to as Central Franconian dialects, constitute a subgroup of West Germanic varieties within the broader West Central German dialect continuum.[1] They are spoken primarily in the Rhineland regions of western and central Germany (including North Rhine-Westphalia, Rhineland-Palatinate, and Saarland), eastern Belgium, Luxembourg, and southeastern Netherlands, forming a transitional zone in the Dutch-German dialect continuum.
